title: Like those who dream (Psalm 126)
hookLine: those who sow in tears shall reap in joy
carry: sow in tears, reap in joy

cards: The phone rings. The scan came back clear. Or: the visa was approved.
Or: they found him, he's safe. For a few seconds the person holding the phone can't take it in. A laugh comes out that's half crying.
Say it again. News this good seems like the kind of thing you wake up from. Psalm one hundred twenty-six begins in exactly that moment, for a whole people.
Something they had stopped expecting has happened, and the only word for it is a dream.

teach.h: AWAKE, BUT IT FEELS LIKE A DREAM
teach.b: Another song of going up, from the pilgrims' collection.
In the King James Bible: "When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream. Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing."

Some readers hear the return from exile in Babylon here, when the Persian king Cyrus let the deported families go home. Some scholars translate the Hebrew more broadly, as when the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion.
Either way, the dreamers aren't asleep. They're wide awake, and it's too good to believe. Even the nations say: the Lord has done great things for them.
Then, in verse four, the mood shifts.
"Turn again our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the south." The south is the Negev, desert country. Its stream beds lie dry, until a heavy rain fills them with rushing water.
So the people are asking for it again. The first homecoming wasn't the end of the hard part.
Then the farmer's line: "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him."

Why would a farmer weep while sowing? Some readers picture a hungry year, when every handful of seed thrown into the ground is a handful you can't eat. Planting is an act of hope that costs something now.

teach.h: SOW IN TEARS, BRING THE SHEAVES
teach.b: The psalm doesn't skip the tears.

teach.h: THEY THAT SOW IN TEARS SHALL REAP IN JOY.
teach.b: It promises the same farmer comes home with his arms full of sheaves. The gospel hymn Bringing in the Sheaves grew from this verse.

how: Christians often pray Psalm 126 in times of waiting and loss, and its sowing verse is sung in hymns such as "Bringing in the Sheaves"; Jewish families sing it before the grace after meals on Sabbaths and festivals.

games.q: you're a farmer in a hungry year, holding the last of your grain. you could eat it, or plant it. what does the psalm's farmer do?
o: go out weeping and sow the seed.
games.why: "he that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing." planting costs something now.

practice: Think of a hard place in your life, a dry stream bed, and choose one small seed to put into it: a kind word, a first step on something you've been putting off, a hope you've been too tired to name.
Hold it the way a farmer holds seed before throwing it. If you pray, offer it to God; if you don't, just plant it on purpose.

wordCard.voice: Negev. The desert country in the south, whose dry streams suddenly rushing with rain is this psalm's picture of being restored.
